Questions

Questions women ask

Is this medical advice?

No. The check describes how you are doing and suggests small, everyday steps. It does not diagnose anything. If you feel very low, it points you to your GP or midwife.

What happens to my answers?

Your result is worked out on your phone. Your answers are only kept if you join the waitlist and say yes to keeping them, and you can have them deleted at any time.

How long does it take?

About two minutes. Eight short questions, one on each screen.

Is it free?

Yes, the check is free.

    Cookies

    This site uses no cookies and no tracking pixels, so there is nothing to accept or reject.

    How visits are counted

    The check counts finished checks and results anonymously on the server, without cookies and without identifying anyone.

    If this ever changes

    Nothing that needs cookies will be added without asking you first, with a clear choice to say no.

    Privacy notice

    A short summary in plain words. The full privacy policy will be added before launch.

    Who is responsible

    Capacity Lab, founded by Georgianna Andrei. Contact details will be added before launch.

    What is collected

    • Anonymous counts of checks started and finished, the result type, season and link source. Nothing that identifies you.
    • If you join the waitlist, your first name and email.
    • Only if you say yes, your check answers, which count as health data.

    Where and how long

    • Stored in the EU.
    • Kept until you unsubscribe. Check answers are deleted after 24 months at the latest.

    Your rights

    You can see, correct, export or delete your data, and withdraw either consent at any time, with one email.

    Behind the scenes

    What happens when a woman taps your link

    1. She opens the check from InstagramEach link you share carries its own tag (bio, story, partner), so you can see what works. Tested inside Instagram’s own browser.
    2. She answers eight questionsHer result is worked out on her phone. Only anonymous counts are sent, so no tracking cookies and no cookie banner. She can skip the personal questions.
    3. She sees her result straight awayScored the same way every time, with one next step and a gentle care note when she is low. She can also send one small ask to someone she trusts, in one tap; nothing is sent for her.
    4. She chooses to joinEmail notes, and, separately and optionally, keeping her wellbeing answers. GDPR treats those answers as health data, so that consent stands on its own.
    5. Stored in the EUA secure database in the EU, holding only what she agreed to.
    6. She confirms, then gets your welcome emailDouble opt-in, sent from your own domain with authentication, so it lands in the inbox.
    7. You see it on your dashboardResults, seasons, sources and sign-ups, with export and deletion on request.

    Built to be safe from day one

    • Wellness wording only, never diagnosis
    • Separate, explicit consent for wellbeing answers
    • Data kept in the EU, only what is needed
    • Privacy notice, consent records and an 18+ confirmation
    • Link previews for Instagram and WhatsApp
    • Fonts hosted with the site, nothing sent to third parties
    • Spam and bot protection on the form

    Checked before launch

    • Every result path tested, including ties
    • iPhone, Android and the Instagram in-app browser
    • Large text, dark mode and screen readers
    • Emails tested in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail
    • You approve it live before anything is invoiced

    Your first 30 days after launch

    1. Week 1. Launch to your followersOne post and a few stories with the link, ready to copy from your Launch kit. Every woman who shares her result card brings the next one in.
    2. Week 2. ListenRead what women chose, ask five of them for one line of feedback, and adjust the words.
    3. Week 3. First partnersSend the partner message from your Launch kit to three midwives or postnatal studios, give each their own link, and see who brings women in.
    4. Week 4. Decide what’s nextYour dashboard shows the most common weak pillar and how many joined. That tells you what to write, and when to open founding memberships.

    Aim for your first 100 women on the waitlist in the first month.

    Where this grows next

    1. Now: the Capacity CheckThe check, results and your waitlist. Every woman’s season and weakest pillar tell you what to create first.
    2. Next: the member spaceHer own login, her result over time, a guided path through your pillars, a weekly note for her season and a monthly re-check.
    3. Then: partners and growthCo-branded links for midwives, postnatal studios and employers, with anonymous group insights, so partners bring women to you.
    4. Later: the full platformPartner logins, paid memberships, a small moderated circle of women in the same season, and a second language, all built on the same data, so nothing is thrown away.
